questions.question:
The demand and production for five businesses V, W, X, Y, and Z are shown in the accompanying chart, which illustrates them using a basic bar graph to provide an answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8f20e8288fa56f49e26dd74b917792c7857c2bc4362cee7b51f90f86f9aceb1a.png] 

The difference between average demand and average production of the four companies (V, W, X, Y) taken together, is:
questions.solution:
**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of values) / (Number of values)

Difference = Average Demand - Average Production

**Calculations:**

Demand for V = 2400

Demand for W = 400

Demand for X = 2000

Demand for Y = 1200

Total Demand (V, W, X, Y) = 2400 + 400 + 2000 + 1200 = 6000

⇒ Average Demand = 6000 / 4 = **1500**

Production for V = 1200

Production for W = 1600

Production for X = 800

Production for Y = 2000

Total Production (V, W, X, Y) = 1200 + 1600 + 800 + 2000 = 5600

⇒ Average Production = 5600 / 4 = **1400**

Difference = Average Demand - Average Production

⇒ Difference = 1500 - 1400 = **100**

The difference between average demand and average production of the four companies (V, W, X, Y) taken together, is **100.**

questions.question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 6% per year rate of interest for 2 years.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹2500

Rate of Interest (R) = 6% per year

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

**Calculation:**

SI = (2500 × 6 × 2) / 100

⇒ SI = (2500 × 12) / 100

⇒ SI = 300

**The simple interest is ₹300.**

questions.question:
What fraction of space will a spherical ball of radius 2.1 cm take in a big spherical container of diameter of 84 cm? 

Take pi = frac{22}7
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the spherical ball = 2.1 cm

Diameter of the spherical container = 84 cm

Radius of the spherical container = 84 / 2 = 42 cm

**Formula Used:**

Fraction of space taken = Volume of the spherical ball / Volume of the spherical container

Volume of a sphere = (4/3) x π x r³

**Calculation:**

Volume of the spherical ball = (4/3) x (22/7) x (2.1)³

⇒ (4/3) x (22/7) x 2.1 x 2.1 x 2.1

⇒ (4/3) x (22/7) x 9.261

⇒ (4 x 22 x 9.261) / (3 x 7)

⇒ 814.968 / 21

⇒ 38.812 cm³

Volume of the spherical container = (4/3) x (22/7) x (42)³

⇒ (4/3) x (22/7) x 42 x 42 x 42

⇒ (4/3) x (22/7) x 74088

⇒ (4 x 22 x 74088) / (3 x 7)

⇒ 6515712 / 21

⇒ 310272 cm³

Fraction of space taken = Volume of the spherical ball / Volume of the spherical container

⇒ 38.812 / 310272

⇒ 1 / 8000

**The fraction of space taken by the spherical ball is 1/8000.**

questions.question: The marks obtained by A in Mathematics, English and Biology are 71 out of 100, 82 out of 150 and 177 out of 200, respectively. What is the average score?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marks obtained by A in Mathematics = 71 out of 100.

Marks obtained by A in English = 82 out of 150.

Marks obtained by A in Biology = 177 out of 200.

**Formula Used:**

Average score = (Sum of marks obtained in all subjects) / (Sum of total marks of all subjects).

**Calculation:**

Sum of marks obtained = 71 + 82 + 177 = 330.

Sum of total marks = 100 + 150 + 200 = 450.

Average score = (330 / 450).

⇒ Average score = (11 / 15).

**The average score is (11 / 15).**

questions.question: If Mohan's income is 20% less than Arvind's income, then how much per cent is Arvind's income more than Mohan's income?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mohan's income is 20% less than Arvind's income.

**Formula Used:**

If one value is x% less than another, the other value is ((x)/(100-x)) × 100 % more.

**Calculation:**

Let Arvind's income be 100.

Then Mohan's income = 100 - 20 = 80.

Arvind's income is more than Mohan's income by:

⇒ ((100 - 80)/(80)) × 100

⇒ (20/80) × 100

⇒ 0.25 × 100

⇒ 25%

**Arvind's income is 25% more than Mohan's income.**

**The correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question: A train travelling at a speed of 36 km/h crosses a pole in 24 sec. What is the length of the train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the train = 36 km/h

Time taken to cross the pole = 24 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Length of the train = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Convert speed to m/s:

Speed = 36 km/h = (36 × 1000) / (60 × 60) m/s

⇒ Speed = 10 m/s

Calculate the length of the train:

Length = Speed × Time

⇒ Length = 10 × 24

⇒ Length = 240 m

**The length of the train is 240 meters.**

questions.question: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 11 and 3465, respectively. If one of the two numbers is 693, what is the other number?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

HCF of two numbers = 11

LCM of two numbers = 3465

One number = 693

**Formula Used:**

HCF × LCM = Product of two numbers

**Calculation:**

Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM

⇒ Product of two numbers = 11 × 3465

⇒ Product of two numbers = 38115

Let the second number be x.

First number × Second number = Product of two numbers

⇒ 693 × x = 38115

⇒ x = 38115 / 693

⇒ x = 55

**The other number is 55.**

questions.question: A clothing store announces a discount scheme 'Buy one shirt and get 40% off on another shirt of the same price'. What is the profit percentage of the store, given that each shirt has a cost price 60% below the marked price?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of each shirt = 60% below Marked Price (MP).

Discount Scheme: "Buy one shirt and get 40% off on another shirt of the same price."

**Formula Used:**

Profit Percentage = [(Selling Price (SP) - Cost Price (CP)) / Cost Price (CP)] × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the Marked Price (MP) of each shirt = ₹100 (Assumed value).

Cost Price (CP) of each shirt = MP × (1 - 60%)

⇒ ₹100 × 0.4 = ₹40.

Total Cost Price (CP) for two shirts = ₹40 + ₹40 = **₹80.**

In the discount scheme, the customer buys two shirts:

Price of first shirt = ₹100 (No discount).

Price of second shirt = ₹100 × (1 - 40%) = ₹100 × 0.6 = ₹60.

Total Selling Price (SP) for two shirts = ₹100 + ₹60 = **₹160.**

Profit = SP - CP = ₹160 - ₹80 = ₹80.

Profit Percentage = (Profit / CP) × 100

⇒ (₹80 / ₹80) × 100 = 100%.

**The profit percentage of the store is 100%.**

questions.question:
The curved surface area of a solid cylinder is 605 cm². The circumference of its base is 22 cm. The total surface area is how many times the height of the cylinder?

Take pi = frac{22}7
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Curved surface area (CSA) of the cylinder = 605 cm²

Circumference of its base = 22 cm

Let the height of the cylinder be h cm, and the radius of its base be r cm.

**Formula Used:**

CSA = 2πrh

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2πr(r + h)

**Calculation:**

From the CSA formula:

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r × h = 605

⇒ (44/7) × r × h = 605

⇒ r × h = (605 × 7) / 44 = **96.25**

From the circumference formula:

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r = 22

⇒ (44/7) × r = 22

⇒ r = 3.5 cm

Substitute r = 3.5 in r × h = 96.25:

⇒ 3.5 × h = 96.25

⇒ h = 96.25 / 3.5 = **27.5 cm**

Total Surface Area (TSA):

⇒ TSA = 2πr(r + h)

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × (3.5 + 27.5)

⇒ (44/7) × 3.5 × 31

⇒ TSA =** 682 cm²**

Ratio of TSA to height:

⇒ TSA / h = 682 / 27.5 = **24.8**

The total surface area is **24.8** times the height of the cylinder.

questions.question: Two trains are running in opposite directions at the same speed. If the length of each train is 150 m and they cross each other in 15 sec, find the speed of each train (in km/hr).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of each train = 150 m

Time taken to cross each other = 15 sec

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = (Sum of the lengths of trains) / Time taken

Speed of each train = Relative Speed / 2

1 m/s = 18/5 km/hr

**Calculation:**

Sum of the lengths of the trains = 150 + 150 = 300 m

Relative Speed = 300 / 15 = 20 m/s

Speed of each train = 20 / 2

⇒ Speed of each train = 10 m/s

Speed in km/hr = 10 × 18/5 

⇒ Speed in km/hr = 36 km/hr

**Speed of each train is 36 km/hr.**

questions.question: In an examination, the average score of a student was 71.9. If the student would have got 28 more marks in English, 22 more marks in Mathematics, 16 more marks in Computer Science, 14 more marks in History, 10 less marks in Hindi, and retained the same marks in other subjects, then the average score would have been 80.65. How many subjects were there in the examination?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial average score of student = 71.9

Change in marks for English = +28

Change in marks for Mathematics = +22

Change in marks for Computer Science = +16

Change in marks for History = +14

Change in marks for Hindi = -10

Final average score = 80.65

**Formula Used:**

Average score = Total marks / Number of subjects

**Calculation:**

Let the number of subjects = n

Total initial marks = 71.9 × n

Total changes in marks = 28 + 22 + 16 + 14 - 10 = 70

Total final marks = Total initial marks + Total changes in marks

Total final marks = (71.9 × n) + 70

Final average score = Total final marks / n

⇒ 80.65 = [(71.9 × n) + 70] / n

⇒ 80.65 × n = (71.9 × n) + 70

⇒ 80.65n - 71.9n = 70

⇒ 8.75n = 70

⇒ n = 70 / 8.75

⇒ n = 8

**The number of subjects in the examination is 8.**

questions.question: If 80 workers took 25 days to finish a task, how many days will it take to finish the same task if 20 more workers join?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number of workers initially = 80

Number of days taken initially = 25

Number of workers after 20 join = 80 + 20 = 100

**Formula Used:**

Work = Total workers × Days

**Calculation:**

Work done by 80 workers in 25 days = 80 × 25

Work done = 2000 units

Let the number of days taken by 100 workers be x.

Work done by 100 workers in x days = 100 × x

Equating the work:

⇒ 100 × x = 2000

⇒ x = 2000 / 100

⇒ x = 20 days

**The correct answer is option 4 (20 days).**

400 chickooes were bought at ₹1280 per hundred and were sold at a profit of ₹980. Find the selling price (in ₹) per dozen of chickooes.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total chickooes bought = 400

Cost price per hundred chickooes = ₹1280

Profit = ₹980

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = (Cost price per hundred × Total chickooes) / 100

Selling Price (SP) of total chickooes = Cost Price + Profit

Selling Price per dozen = (Selling Price of total chickooes × 12) / Total chickooes

**Calculation:**

Cost Price (CP) of total chickooes:

CP = (₹1280 × 400) / 100

⇒ CP = ₹5120

Selling Price (SP) of total chickooes:

SP = CP + Profit

⇒ SP = ₹5120 + ₹980

⇒ SP = ₹6100

Now,

Selling Price per dozen = (SP × 12) / Total chickooes

⇒ (₹6100 × 12) / 400 = ₹183

**The selling price per dozen of chickooes is ₹183.**

questions.question: The area of a right-angled triangle is 80m². If its perpendicular is equal to 20 m, then find its base.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Area of the triangle = 80 m²

Perpendicular = 20 m

**Formula Used:**

Area of a right-angled triangle = (1/2) × Base × Perpendicular

**Calculation:**

Using the formula:

Area = (1/2) × Base × Perpendicular

⇒ 80 = (1/2) × Base × 20

⇒ Base = 80 / 10 = 8 m

**The base of the triangle is 8 m.**

questions.question: Mr Rao purchased a laptop for ₹45,000. After a few months, as his office provided another laptop, he sold it at a loss of 12% to Mrs Sharma. After one year, she sold it to an engineering student for a profit of 12%. What is the amount the student had to pay?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price of laptop for Mr Rao = ₹45,000

Loss percentage when sold to Mrs Sharma = 12%

Profit percentage when Mrs Sharma sold to an engineering student = 12%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 ± Percentage/100)

**Calculation:**

Selling price when Mr Rao sold the laptop to Mrs Sharma

Loss = 12%

⇒ Selling Price = ₹45,000 × (1 - 12/100)

⇒ ₹45,000 × 0.88 = ₹39,600

Selling price when Mrs Sharma sold the laptop to the engineering student

Profit = 12%

⇒ Selling Price = ₹39,600 × (1 + 12/100)

⇒ ₹39,600 × 1.12 = ₹44,352

The amount the engineering student had to pay is** ₹44,352.**
